claims: Artemis II is the first crewed mission of NASA's Artemis program.
Artemis II is scheduled to take approximately four to five days to reach the moon.
The crew of Artemis II will enter the lunar vicinity around day five.
The total mission duration of Artemis II is roughly 10 days.
Artemis II will fly around the moon before returning to Earth.
Artemis II includes crewed travel to the far side of the moon.
The Orion spacecraft will travel at speeds up to 24,500 mph (39,400 km/h) to escape Earth's gravity before slowing down and being pulled in by the Moon's gravity.
Artemis II will take the crew 252,000 miles from Earth.
Artemis II will set a record for the farthest humans have traveled into space.
Artemis II will make one pass around the moon.
The return trip to Earth for Artemis II is expected to take another three to four days.
The CBS News update and NASA official blog note that the projected Artemis II mission timeline is scheduled for April 2026.
